html:
A small Germanic people, among the earliest named in written sources: an inscription from the Greek city of Olbia mentions them threatening it around 200 BCE. The map shows them in 400 north of the Black Sea, near Olbia.

In the 5th century the Sciri were part of Attila's empire. After it broke up in the 450s they set up a short-lived kingdom on the middle Danube, which the Ostrogoths destroyed around 469. Their most famous member was probably Odoacer, son of a Scirian chief, who in 476 deposed the last western Roman emperor. Their neighbours included the Heruli and the Huns.
